about: Own-words reads from the daily research task (ADMIS, Rabobank, Czapp and the news feed). fund_score: -1 bearish to +1 bullish, a judgement on the fundamental news only.

corn.fundamental: Dec recovers to ~439 (+0.8%) with a softer dollar and firmer crude, but weekly export sales fell from recent highs, so the demand story is cooling while fund selling has paused rather than reversed.
events: Weekly corn export sales decline (Dow Jones)
Chicago grains regain ground as dollar and oil ease pressure (Reuters)
Brazil's corn ethanol boom is speeding feedlot beef growth (Reuters)

soybeans.fundamental: Jan slips to ~1,210 (-0.5%) despite higher weekly export sales; reports of China holding imported beans at ports with swelling domestic stocks undercut hopes of bigger US buying before the trade talks.
events: US soybean export sales rise on the week (Dow Jones)
China holds soybean imports at ports as domestic supplies swell (Bloomberg, Farm Progress)
Strong crush demand supports basis (Brownfield)

meal.fundamental: Meal gives back a little (-0.4%) as soyoil firms with crude; heavy crush keeps meal supply ample, so its relative strength depends on oil staying weak.
events: Soymeal the outlier on Wednesday (ADMIS)
Strong crush pace (Brownfield)

oil.fundamental: Soyoil firms ~0.9% to ~60.4 with crude; supply from the heavy crush is ample, so the energy link remains the main driver.
events: Crude up on Middle East risk (Dow Jones)
Soyoil fell below support Wednesday (Barchart)

wheat.fundamental: A second day of short covering lifts Dec to ~578 (+1.4%), helped by better weekly export sales (~345k t); nothing changes the heavy supply backdrop of Black Sea truce hopes and improving US winter-wheat moisture.
events: Wheat export sales 345k t for 26/27 (USDA via Dow Jones)
Grains recover ground after broad selloff (Dow Jones)
El Niño seen improving the US winter wheat outlook (Brownfield)

kc.fundamental: HRW leads again: Dec ~626 (+2.7%), back above 615.5 resistance. It reads as short covering out of oversold levels; Plains moisture is still a supply positive for the 2027 crop.
events: KC Dec up ~16.75 to ~626 (CBOT via TradingView)
Wheat export sales improve (Dow Jones)
El Niño improving US winter wheat outlook (Brownfield)

cotton.fundamental: Old-crop has bounced with Dec back to ~76 (+1.4%) and Mar near 80 despite a firm dollar, a technical recovery rather than new supply news. Dec deliveries and the high-grade share of certificated stock still cap the comfort for longs until Mar is the lead month.
events: Strong dollar weighed on cotton early (ADMIS)
Dec ~76.0, Mar ~79.8 by midday (ICE via TradingView)
Texas yield trimmed again in USDA's November report (RFD-TV)

hogs.fundamental: Dec bounces ~1.6% to ~52.2 off contract lows; the Thailand deal's pork access and $2.6bn of ag purchases help sentiment, but they are small and slow against heavy current supplies.
events: Thailand trade deal to include $2.6bn of US ag purchases and pork access (Successful Farming)
Lean hogs set new contract lows this week (ADMIS, Barchart)

cattle.fundamental: Dec firms ~1.1% to ~222 while cash trade is awaited. Tyson adding Texas beef capacity through the Allied Beef deal points to more packer demand for scarce cattle; supply stays tight.
events: Tyson boosts Texas beef capacity with Allied Beef deal (Farm Progress)
Tyson's beef segment still a drag on earnings (Barron's)
USDA restricts European ruminant germplasm as Shamonda virus spreads (Feedstuffs)

feeders.fundamental: Feeders firmed (~+0.9%) with the cash index near 338 and corn at lows supporting feeding margins; smaller December daily limits are coming.
events: CME to reduce feeder cattle daily limits in December (DTN)
Corn near new lows lowers feed costs (Successful Farming)

class3.fundamental: Dec Class III steadies near 17.0 after the block-led drop; US dairy exports on track for another record year are a demand support, but cheese supply keeps spot prices heavy.
events: US dairy exports heading for another record year (Dairy Herd)
Cheese blocks led losses Wednesday (Brownfield)

class4.fundamental: Record-pace dairy exports support NDM and butter demand; the Class IV nowcast still sits above futures on firm powder.
events: US dairy exports heading for another record year (Dairy Herd)
Dairy prices lower Wednesday (Brownfield)

palm.fundamental: Jan rebounds ~0.8% to ~4,288 with firmer crude and soyoil; no new supply data, so it is following the vegoil complex.
events: Jan ~4,288 (+35) (Bursa via TradingView)
Crude and soyoil higher (TradingView)

natgas.fundamental: Dec extends losses to ~3.30 (-2.1%) and stays below 3.342 support; slower LNG flows through Hormuz support US cargo demand, but storage ending the season above normal limits the upside.
events: Natgas Dec ~3.30, below 3.342 support (NYMEX via TradingView)
LNG exports through Hormuz slow after more attacks (Bloomberg)
US storage ended injection season above normal (EIA)

crude.fundamental: WTI holds ~84.4 (+1.3%): mine strikes and attacks around Hormuz plus Marathon's force majeure on North Dakota deliveries offset the surplus talk; the market still swings between Gulf shipping risk and ample supply.
events: Oil futures pick up as Middle East risks remain (Dow Jones)
Marathon declares force majeure on North Dakota oil deliveries (Seeking Alpha)
Brent holds on Hormuz mine strikes (Invezz)

ulsd.fundamental: Diesel slips ~0.5% to ~3.95 while crude firms; stocks are well below normal and cracks wide, but more barrels arriving, including a Russian-diesel tanker that briefly signalled a US port, and Bapco's restart lean bearish.
events: Tanker carrying Russian diesel briefly signalled a US port (Dow Jones/Kpler)
Bapco refinery heading back to full capacity (Reuters)
Distillate stocks stay below normal (EIA)

rbob.fundamental: RBOB edges up with crude, but last week's large gasoline build and stocks above normal keep the seasonal-demand picture soft.
events: Gasoline stocks rose 5.2 mb, above the 5-year norm (EIA)
Crude rebounds on Hormuz attacks (OilPrice.com)
